title: Email Marketing for Small B2B Teams — Jon Martin
seoTitle: Email Marketing Tools for Small B2B Teams
description: Transpond, Brevo, and ActiveCampaign compared for small B2B teams: entry prices, free plans and trials, users included, and automation.
h1: Email marketing for a small B2B team
dek: Three email marketing tools for a B2B team that sends a newsletter, a few nurture sequences, and the odd product announcement, without a marketing department.
Prices and features below come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown.

blocks.html: This is for a B2B company with a small list, often a few hundred to a few thousand contacts, where one or two people handle marketing on top of other work.
If you already run {{link:hubspot}} for sales, you may be weighing its marketing tools against a separate email platform. This page covers the separate-platform side, priced for a small list.

Start with Brevo if you want to send for free while the list is small. Pick Transpond if you want a low monthly price with several users and unlimited automations. Pick ActiveCampaign if automation is the heart of what you do and you're comfortable paying for it.
All three price by list size or email volume, so the number on the pricing page only holds for the list size it was quoted at. Re-price at the size you expect a year from now.
Transpond Starter is {{fact:transpond.starter}}. Growth is {{fact:transpond.growth}}. There's also {{fact:transpond.free}}, and {{fact:transpond.annual}}.
Transpond also offers {{fact:transpond.ai}}. One limit to know: Transpond offers {{fact:transpond.sms}}.
Brevo has {{fact:brevo.free}}. Starter is {{fact:brevo.starter}}, and Standard is {{fact:brevo.standard}}. Per Brevo, {{fact:brevo.annual}}.
Seats are tight on the lower plans: Brevo lists {{fact:brevo.seats}}. Contacts are tied to email volume, with {{fact:brevo.contacts}}.
ActiveCampaign Starter is {{fact:activecampaign.starter}}. Plus is {{fact:activecampaign.plus}}. Pro is {{fact:activecampaign.pro}}. There's {{fact:activecampaign.trial}}.
ActiveCampaign gives you {{fact:activecampaign.templates}}. The pricing page shows {{fact:activecampaign.scaling}}, so a bigger list moves you up fast.
Count users first. If two or three people need to build campaigns, check the seat limit on the plan before the price. A cheap plan with one seat means sharing a login, which you shouldn't do.
Then list the automations you'll actually build in the first quarter: a welcome series, a demo follow-up, a re-engagement email. If that's the whole list, you don't need the most advanced builder.
Last, decide how contacts move between your CRM and the email tool. If sales lives in HubSpot, look for a sync or an integration before you import a single list.
Set up SPF, DKIM, and DMARC on your sending domain before the first campaign. Every tool here will walk you through it, and skipping it hurts deliverability from day one.
Import only contacts who agreed to hear from you, and keep the unsubscribe link visible.

faq.q: Which is cheapest for a small list?
faq.a: Transpond Starter is {{fact:transpond.starter}}. Brevo Starter is {{fact:brevo.starter}}.

faq.q: How many users do I get?
faq.a: Transpond Starter has up to 3 users. Brevo lists {{fact:brevo.seats}}. ActiveCampaign Pro includes 3 user seats.

faq.q: Can I send SMS from these?
faq.a: Transpond offers {{fact:transpond.sms}}. Check Brevo and ActiveCampaign pricing pages for SMS add-ons in your country.

closing: Pick the cheapest plan that gives every sender a seat and covers the automations you'll build this quarter, then re-price as the list grows.
